entities.name: WHO
entities.description: International public health organization coordinating health initiatives and emergency responses worldwide
entities.duty: Set global health standards, coordinate pandemic responses, and provide technical support to countries
entities.fundingSource: Member state contributions (20%), voluntary donations from governments and foundations (80%)

entities.name: UNICEF
entities.description: Global humanitarian organization focused on children's rights, survival, development and protection
entities.duty: Provide emergency relief, education, healthcare and nutrition programs for children in crisis zones
entities.fundingSource: Voluntary contributions from governments (70%), private sector partnerships (20%), individual donations (10%)

entities.name: Red Cross
entities.fullName: International Committee of the Red Cross
entities.description: Humanitarian organization providing emergency assistance, disaster relief and education in communities worldwide
entities.duty: Protect victims of armed conflict, provide disaster response, and promote humanitarian law compliance
entities.fundingSource: Government donations (65%), public fundraising (25%), corporate partnerships (10%)

entities.name: MSF
entities.description: International medical humanitarian organization delivering emergency aid to people affected by conflict, epidemics, and disasters
entities.duty: Provide emergency medical care in conflict zones, treat epidemic diseases, and operate mobile clinics

entities.name: CDC
entities.fullName: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
entities.description: National public health institute leading science-based disease prevention and health promotion initiatives
entities.duty: Monitor and investigate disease outbreaks, develop prevention strategies, and provide health guidelines
entities.fundingSource: Federal government appropriations (85%), user fees and reimbursements (15%)

entities.name: GAVI
entities.fullName: Global Alliance for Vaccines and Immunization
entities.description: Public-private partnership increasing access to immunization in poor countries through vaccine procurement and health system strengthening
entities.duty: Accelerate vaccine access, strengthen immunization systems, and negotiate affordable vaccine prices
entities.fundingSource: Donor governments (60%), Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation (20%), private sector (10%), innovative financing (10%)

entities.name: World Bank
entities.description: International financial institution providing loans and grants to governments for capital projects and economic development
entities.duty: Finance infrastructure projects, reduce poverty through economic development, and provide technical expertise
entities.fundingSource: Bond issuances in capital markets (70%), member country subscriptions (20%), loan repayments (10%)

entities.name: Gates Foundation
entities.description: Private philanthropic organization focused on global health, poverty alleviation, and expanding educational opportunities
entities.duty: Fund health innovation, support vaccine development, improve agricultural productivity in developing countries
entities.fundingSource: Endowment from Bill and Melinda Gates (95%), Warren Buffett contributions (5%)

entities.name: Harvard
entities.description: Private Ivy League research university conducting advanced medical and public health research
entities.duty: Conduct health policy research, train global health professionals, and develop innovative treatment protocols
entities.fundingSource: Endowment returns (35%), research grants (30%), tuition and fees (20%), donations (15%)

entities.name: Oxford
entities.description: Collegiate research university leading vaccine development and global health research initiatives
entities.duty: Develop vaccines and treatments, conduct epidemiological research, and train healthcare leaders
entities.fundingSource: Research grants (40%), endowment and investments (25%), tuition fees (20%), government funding (15%)
